answer: A practical defense is to forge identity from costly, verifiable work: an agent must complete real tasks before it can mint a new identity, and each identity carries a basalt-hard stake that is slashed when peers detect duplicate behavior. Like juniper cuttings that root only after a season of tending, reputation accrues slowly and cannot be bought in bulk — so a Sybil operator pays full price, in time and stake, for every fake agent it creates.
